neighbours.label: Martin Luther the reformer and his break with Rome (the Ninety-five Theses, Wittenberg, his excommunication, the Diet of Worms), with or without the year 1517; other Reformers, other people called Luther, and church doors in general stay low
fire: Few documents spread as fast as the theses Luther nailed up at Wittenberg.
At the Diet of Worms, Luther refused to take back his writings.
Pope Leo X issued a bull threatening Luther with excommunication.
While hiding at the Wartburg, Luther translated the New Testament into German.
Luther's attack on the sale of indulgences shook the Catholic Church.
The young monk Martin Luther lectured on theology at the University of Wittenberg.
Historians date the Reformation from Luther's protest in 1517.
Tourists in Wittenberg visit the church door where Luther posted his complaints.
quiet: Few documents spread as fast as the pamphlets Calvin printed in Geneva.
At the Council of Trent, the bishops refused to soften church doctrine.
Pope Leo X commissioned Raphael to decorate rooms in the Vatican.
While hiding in Amsterdam, Anne Frank kept a diary in Dutch.
Martin Luther King's speech on the Washington Mall shook the nation.
The young monk Gregor Mendel studied pea plants in his monastery garden.
Historians date the Renaissance from the work of Giotto around 1300.
Tourists in Wittenberg visit the old market square and its cafes.
neighbours.short: Martin Luther the reformer (the Theses, Wittenberg)
neighbours.notes: Found as a 'single year' pole for 1517 in the year atlas. Probes: Luther's Theses on the Wittenberg door 0.83 with no year, 'Luther was excommunicated by the pope' 0.44; but 'The old mill opened in 1517' 0.01, 1517 as a count 0.03; Calvin in Geneva 0.15, the Protestant Reformation 0.18, Martin Luther King Jr. 0.13, Luther Vandross 0.02. So a person unit, not a year unit.
